title: Reflexive 10: The Passive Use (дом строится)
description: The -ся marker can make a sentence passive: the subject is the thing that the action happens to. Дом строится means 'The house is being built.' If you name who does it, that doer goes in the instrumental: строится рабочими.
descriptionRussian: Показатель -ся может сделать предложение страдательным: подлежащее — это то, с чем происходит действие. «Дом строится» значит 'дом строят'. Если назвать того, кто делает действие, он стоит в творительном падеже: «строится рабочими».
intro: A third job for the ending, and the most useful one for reading. Adding it lets a sentence describe something being done without naming who is doing it: the house is being built, the book reads easily. Russian reaches for this constantly in signs, notices and news, so recognizing it matters more than producing it at this stage.
rules: Add -ся to make the sentence passive: the subject becomes the thing the action happens to. Дом строится = the house is being built.
The doer is usually left out. When you name the doer, put it in the instrumental case (the кем? case): строится рабочими.
The verb still agrees with its subject: singular subject takes the singular ending (дом строится), plural subject takes the plural ending (дома строятся).
This passive use is most common with imperfective verbs in the present and past (строится, строился, читается, читался).
examples: Дом строится рядом с парком. (The house is being built next to the park.) Subject дом undergoes the action; no doer named.
Дом строится рабочими. (The house is being built by workers.) The doer рабочими is in the instrumental.
Книга читается легко. (The book reads easily.) Passive use; the book is the thing being read.
Завтрак подаётся в восемь часов. (Breakfast is served at eight o'clock.) Common on signs and timetables.
Письмо пишется секретарём. (The letter is being written by the secretary.) Doer секретарём in the instrumental.
Новые дома строятся быстро. (The new houses are being built quickly.) Plural subject дома → plural ending строятся.

tables.title: Active vs Passive (same news, two angles)

items.promptEnglish: A new house is being built next to the park.
items.hint: The house is the thing the action happens to. Which form carries -ся?
items.explanation: Passive use: дом is the subject and undergoes the action, so the verb takes -ся → строится.

items.hint: The book is read; the readers are not named. Add -ся.
items.explanation: Passive use: книга is the thing being read, so the verb takes -ся → читается.

items.promptEnglish: Breakfast is served from eight in the morning.
items.hint: A timetable line. The breakfast is the subject of the action.
items.explanation: Passive use, common on signs and timetables: завтрак is the subject undergoing the action → подаётся.

items.promptEnglish: The house is being built by workers.
items.hint: When you name the doer in a passive sentence, which case do you use?
items.explanation: In a passive sentence the named doer goes in the instrumental (the кем? case): рабочими.

items.promptEnglish: The letter is being written by the secretary.
items.hint: The doer of a passive action takes the instrumental.
items.explanation: The doer of a passive sentence is in the instrumental: секретарём (answers кем?).

items.promptEnglish: The new houses are being built very quickly.
items.hint: The subject дома is plural. Match the ending.
items.explanation: The verb agrees with its subject: дома is plural, so the passive form takes the plural ending → строятся.

items.hint: The house is not doing the building. Which -ся form?
items.explanation: The passive -ся turns the thing acted on into the subject: дом строится.

items.promptEnglish: The school is being built by workers.
items.hint: The named doer of a -ся passive goes in which case?
items.explanation: The doer of a -ся passive stands in the instrumental: школа строится рабочими.

items.hint: The book is not doing the reading. Which form?
items.explanation: The -ся passive with no doer named: книга читается легко.

blanks: Новая школа _____ в центре города. (A new school is being built in the city centre.)
Этот журнал _____ во всех киосках. (This magazine is sold at every kiosk.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Passive use of -ся. The subjects (школа, журнал) are the things the action happens to, so the verbs take -ся: строится, продаётся.

sentenceBuilding.translation: The house is being built by workers.
sentenceBuilding.hint: Subject first; the named doer goes in the instrumental at the end.
Passive verb with -ся; no doer is named here.
A timetable line: subject, passive verb, then the time.

sentenceBuilding.translation: The article is being written by a journalist.
sentenceBuilding.hint: The named doer (the journalist) goes in the instrumental.

hints: он/она/оно (дом ...): singular subject undergoing the action
они (дома ...): plural subject undergoing the action

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: This house has been for sale for a year already.
errorCorrection.explanation: The house is the thing being sold, so the verb needs -ся → продаётся. The bare продаёт means 'is selling something' and would need a doer-subject plus an object, which the sentence does not have.

errorCorrection.sentence: Дом строится строители за один год.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The house is being built by builders in one year.
errorCorrection.explanation: In a passive sentence the named doer goes in the instrumental (the кем? case): строителями. Строители is the nominative, which would make them the active subject ('the builders build').

errorCorrection.sentence: Эти газеты продаётся в каждом киоске.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: These newspapers are sold at every kiosk.
errorCorrection.explanation: The verb agrees with its subject. Газеты is plural, so the passive form needs the plural ending → продаются. Продаётся is the singular form (for one газета).

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Dinner is still being prepared - wait a little.
errorCorrection.explanation: Ужин is the thing being prepared, so the verb needs -ся → готовится. The bare готовит means 'is cooking something' and would need a doer-subject plus an object.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: A new school is being built in the city centre.
minimalPairs.explanation: Passive use: школа is the thing being built, so the verb takes -ся → строится. Строит is the active form ('is building something') and would need a doer-subject plus an object.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: The house is being built by workers.
minimalPairs.explanation: When the doer is named in a passive sentence, it goes in the instrumental: рабочими. Рабочие is the nominative, which would turn them into the active subject ('the workers are building').
Passive use: книга is the thing being read, so the verb takes -ся → читается. Читает means 'he/she reads (something)' and would need a different subject plus an object.
